title: Launch Watchtower: Cross-team Risk Coordination & Rapid-Rollback Playbook
creator: Lena Cho
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable coordination plan (the 'Watchtower') for the upcoming runtime-1.23 release that centralizes decisioning for blockers, defines rapid rollback criteria and runbook, and provides ready-to-send incident and customer comms templates. This ticket aligns PM, Eng, SRE, Design, and GTM for the release window and establishes a single source of truth for go/no-go calls.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Stakeholder rota and on-call Watchtower owner assigned for the release window. 2) Blocker gating rubric documented and approved by Eng+SRE. 3) Rollback runbook validated in staging (dry-run) and linked. 4) Incident and customer comms templates completed and approved by Legal and Support. 5) Post-launch triage and RCA workflow defined with required dashboards and signal thresholds.
milestones: 2026-02-12 — Draft gating rubric and list of potential blockers
2026-02-18 — Engineering + SRE review and sign-off on rollback runbook
2026-03-03 — Dry-run rollback in staging with canary traffic
2026-03-10 — Final Watchtower sync; publish launch pack and Slack channels
risk_matrix: Risk categories: service stability (memory OOMs, latency regressions), data integrity (KV cache corruption, schema migrations), security (token leakage, KMS failures), UX regressions (structured output breakage), capacity (unexpected autoscale behavior). For each risk we list likelihood, impact, and mitigations in the release pack. Example: latency regression — likelihood: medium, impact: high, mitigation: reduced max_batch_size, immediate fallback to last-known-good model variant, enable degraded-mode caching.
rollback_plan_summary: Primary criteria to trigger rollback: A) sustained 30%+ error rate increase for >5 minutes on production P95 requests for core inference endpoints; B) confirmed data corruption affecting more than 0.5% of persisted entries; C) escalation to SEV-1 by SRE with inability to restore service within 15 minutes. Rollback steps: 1) Watchtower lead declares Rollback, notifies Exec & Support. 2) Trigger automated CI/CD job to revert traffic routing to previous release (tagged runtime-1.22-stable) via deployment manager. 3) If dedicated capacity involved, shift to capacity pool with reserved images. 4) Run post-rollback verification suite (smoke + core regression tests). 5) Open RCA channel and schedule hot-fix cadence. Roles: Eng on-call executes rollback commands, SRE validates infra switches, PM manages comms, Support coordinates customer notifications.
incident_comm_templates:
SEV-1 Incident (internal): Subject: [SEV-1] runtime-1.23 — Service disruption detected
Body: Short summary of impact, what systems are affected, immediate mitigation steps taken, owner, ETA for next update. Example placeholders: Impact: inference API errors 5xx affecting ~X% of requests. Mitigation: rolling rollback initiated to runtime-1.22. Owner: @MarcoRuiz. Next update: in 15 minutes.

SEV-1 Customer Notice (support): Subject: Incident: Temporary degraded service for inference API
Body: We are investigating an incident impacting inference latency/errors. We have reverted to a stable runtime and are monitoring for stability. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. No action required from customers at this time. Contact: support@redwood.ai.

SEV-2 Internal Update: Subject: [SEV-2] runtime-1.23 — Performance regression observed
Body: Brief description, affected metrics, mitigation in progress (throttles, reduced QPS), owner, expected check-in time.

Customer Postmortem Summary (template): Title: Postmortem — runtime-1.23 incident on YYYY-MM-DD
Sections: What happened, Impact, Root cause (high level), Remediation completed, ETA for permanent fix, Customer mitigations, Contact info.
